examples.en: Some salt too, please.
Is there any salt here?

Naengmyeon is very cold.
One bowl of naengmyeon, please.
I add a little vinegar to the naengmyeon.

examples.en: Is the naengmyeon here good? — Yes, it's really good.

explain: 냉면 가게에서는 “면을 잘라 드릴까요?”라고 물어보기도 해요. 긴 면이 불편하면 “잘라 주세요”라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 내가 좋아하는 냉면은 일단 시원한 육수는 기본이고, 메밀로 된 면발이어야 한다.

Samgyetang has ginseng in it.

On the hottest days of summer, people eat samgyetang.
The samgyetang is very hot.

explain: 많은 한국 사람은 더운 여름에 뜨거운 삼계탕을 먹어요. 더운 날 뜨거운 음식으로 힘을 얻는다고 생각해요.

dict_examples.en: I ate samgyetang on a hottest day to boost my health.

examples.en: Galbitang has a delicious broth.
Galbitang is 12,000 won a bowl.
Two bowls of galbitang, please.
I put rice into the galbitang.
This restaurant is famous for galbitang.

explain: 탕은 국물이 많은 음식이에요. 갈비탕은 갈비로 끓인 맑은 국이에요. 불에 구운 “갈비”와 달라요.

dict_examples.en: When I went to the wedding, they served galbitang as the meal.

explain_en: 탕 means a dish with a lot of broth. 갈비탕 is a clear soup boiled with beef short ribs. It is different from grilled 갈비, which has no soup.

examples.en: We eat japchae on birthdays.
We make japchae for the holidays.
One plate of japchae, please.
I put spinach and carrots in the japchae.
Do you make japchae? — Yes, I make it on weekends.

explain: 잡채의 국수는 “당면”이에요. 고구마 가루로 만든 투명한 면이에요. 먹으면 쫀득쫀득해요.

dict_examples.en: Gilsang picks up a piece of meat from the japchae and puts it in the child's mouth.

It's three to nothing right now.

examples.en: It takes twenty minutes from home to school.
Our apartment is on the twentieth floor.
Today is the twentieth.
It's twenty degrees outside right now.
I take bus number twenty.

dict_examples.en: This year I turned twenty.

examples.en: The bus is thirty minutes late.
This bag is 300,000 won.

phrases.nuance_en: running away in a hurry, usually when things suddenly go wrong
phrases.en_equiv: When the rain poured down, everyone ran for it.

explain_en: Thirty minutes can be 삼십 분 or 반 (“half”). 세 시 삼십 분 is also 세 시 반, just like English “half past three”.

dis.h: Sino-Korean number; for minutes, dates, money

p.n: Both work with 명. But with 분 only 삼십 works, and with 살 only 서른.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 아침 사십 분 걸어요.
examples.en: I walk for forty minutes every morning.
Lunch break is forty minutes.
These shoes are 400,000 won.

examples.en: Where does bus number 40 go? — To City Hall.

examples.ko: 사십 도는 너무 더워요. 밖에 안 나가요.
examples.en: Forty degrees is too hot. I don't go outside.

explain: 나이를 말할 때는 ‘사십 살’보다 ‘마흔 살’이라고 해요. 사십은 돈, 분, 번호, 층에 써요: 사십 분, 사십 층.

dict_examples.en: Five times eight is forty.

explain_en: For age, say ‘마흔 살’ rather than ‘사십 살’. Use 사십 for money, minutes, numbers and floors: 사십 분, 사십 층.

dis.h: Sino-Korean number; used for minutes, money

examples.en: Class is fifty minutes long.

examples.en: It's 9:50 now. It's almost ten.

explain: 나이를 말할 때는 ‘오십 살’보다 ‘쉰 살’이라고 해요. 오십은 돈, 분, 번호에 써요: 오십 분, 오십 원.

dict_examples.en: One hundred divided by two is fifty.

dis.h: fifty; Sino-Korean, used for money, dates

p.n: 쉰 원 is wrong; money uses Sino-Korean numbers.

examples.en: One hour is sixty minutes.
This bus is number 60.
My phone battery is at sixty percent.
The airport is sixty kilometers from my home.
My room is number sixty.

explain: 육십은 [육씹]이라고 읽어요. 받침 ㄱ 뒤에서 십의 ㅅ이 센 소리 ㅆ으로 바뀌어요. 쓴 것과 소리가 달라요.

dict_examples.en: A child born after one turned sixty.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 나이 육십에 한글 공부를 시작했다.
dict_examples.en: He started studying Hangeul at the age of sixty.

explain_en: 육십 is pronounced [육씹]. After the final ㄱ of 육, the ㅅ in 십 becomes a tense ㅆ, so it sounds different from how it is written.

dis.h: Sino-Korean sixty, used with won, minutes

p.n: Minutes take Sino-Korean numbers, so the native form does not fit.

examples.en: I'm 170 centimeters tall.
It's seventy kilometers to Grandma's house.

examples.ko: 내일 비가 와요. 확률은 칠십 퍼센트예요.
examples.en: It will rain tomorrow. The chance is seventy percent.
My younger brother weighs seventy kilos.
My test score is seventy points.

explain: 칠십은 [칠씹]이라고 읽어요. 나이를 말할 때는 “일흔 살”이라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 예전에는 초등학교 한 반의 학생 수가 칠십인 적도 있었다.
dict_examples.en: There was a time when one elementary school class had seventy students.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 칠십 is pronounced [칠씹]. For age, say 일흔 살 (native number), not 칠십 살.

dis.h: sino number, for money, pages, dates

p.n: The native number does not go with 쪽.

examples.en: The rent is 800,000 won a month.
This book is eighty pages long.
It is eighty meters from here to the school.
The water is eighty degrees. It's very hot.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 팔십 퍼센트 할인이에요. 정말 싸요!
examples.en: This bag is 80 percent off. It's really cheap!

explain: 팔십은 [팔씹]이라고 읽어요. 받침 ㄹ 뒤에서 십의 ㅅ이 ㅆ 소리가 돼요. 80번째 생일은 “팔순”이에요.

dict_examples.ko: 그의 눈은 팔십 고령답지 않게 빛을 내고 있었다.
dict_examples.en: His eyes shone, unlike those of someone of eighty.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 팔십 is pronounced [팔씹]. After the final ㄹ, the ㅅ of 십 turns into a tense ㅆ sound. An 80th birthday is called 팔순.

dis.h: Sino-Korean number; for money, pages, dates

p.n: Money uses Sino-Korean numbers, so 여든 원 is wrong.

examples.en: This movie is ninety minutes long.

examples.ko: 학교 앞에 구십 번 버스가 와요.
examples.en: The number 90 bus comes to the front of the school.

examples.ko: 저 건물은 구십 층이에요. 정말 높아요!
examples.en: That building has ninety floors. It's really tall!
A tourist visa is ninety days.

examples.ko: 시험 점수가 구십 점이에요. 정말 좋아요!
examples.en: My test score is ninety. That's really good!

explain: 나이는 “아흔 살”이라고 해요. 구십은 점수, 퍼센트, 번호, 층수를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 학생들이 선생님께 구십 도 인사를 해요.
phrases.en: The students bow deeply to the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허리를 깊이 숙여서 아주 공손하게 하는 인사
phrases.nuance_en: a deep bow from the waist, showing great respect
phrases.en_equiv: The students bow deeply to the teacher.

explain_en: For age say 아흔 살 (native number). 구십 is for scores, percentages, numbers and floors.

p.n: 아흔 is the native number for age or counting things, not for page numbers.
